claims.text: Integrating high-throughput MDSC with in-situ high-energy XRD will determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, melting volume change, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties more accurately and efficiently than conventional DSC.
Equimolar CoCrFeMnNi is a representative high-entropy alloy suitable for the proposed protocol in an as-cast, single-phase state.
The proposed protocol combines standard-calibrated MDSC with simultaneous in-situ high-energy XRD during controlled thermal cycling.
Modulation of the heat-flow signal enhances detection of subtle energetic changes associated with phase transitions.
Diffraction-peak shifts enhance detection of structural and volume changes during melting.
MDSC separates reversing and non-reversing heat flow.
Separating reversing and non-reversing heat flow reduces baseline drift and distinguishes latent heat attributable to melting.
Concurrent XRD captures lattice expansion and other structural changes that directly correlate with volume change upon melting.
Synchronizing calorimetry and diffraction ensures that thermal events are accurately mapped to material transformations.
The integrated method is expected to reduce measurement uncertainty by approximately 20–30% relative to conventional DSC.
The integrated method will produce more reliable liquid-phase thermodynamic property data.
Conventional DSC typically suffers from baseline drift and lower resolution for thermal and volume changes at melting.
The approach is most applicable to high-entropy alloys with stable, single-phase microstructures.
Compositionally inhomogeneous or multiphase high-entropy alloys may obtain less precision improvement from the method.
